Same Db7/B7 pair as bars 5-8 and 21-24, now the established motif, so the last chorus feels like the summing-up rather than a new idea.

review.verdict: Bars 1–24: The tritone motif is placed exactly where the plan asks for it: B7alt on every cadential F7 and Db7 on the G7s, giving the chromatic D-Db-C-B descent a recognizable identity, while bars 1-3, 5, 7 and 9-11 stay diatonic so the tune remains legible. The related-ii moves in bars 10 and 12 and the D7 in bar 13 keep the technique mix from collapsing into one device, and the bass line is genuinely smooth at 0.89 with no avoid notes. I found nothing in this part worth trading away — any further substitution would either blur the bars-5-8 / 21-24 mirror or push density and runs for no musical gain, so I leave it as is. Bars 25–44: This part reads as a well-executed realization of the plan: the backdoor phrase at 25-28 is left intact with only a related-ii split of the I7 and the bVII7, the F-E-Eb bass into the bridge is genuinely smooth, and the bridge's chromatic descents (D-Db-C-B, then A-Ab-G-Gb) land with the melody notes as b7s and #11s rather than as clashes. The tritone subs are plentiful but that is the requested style, and the diatonic footholds (Dm7, Cm7, Am7b5, Gm7) keep the ear oriented; the Eb6/9 plateau at bar 34 is a tasteful bit of relief. I found nothing that clearly improves on it, so I am leaving the part unchanged. Bars 45–64: The part reads well: the Db7/B7 pair is consistently in place as the closing motif, the last A stays recognizable, the I7-IV-ivm7-bVII7 plateau is left calm, and the final bass D-Db-C-B-Bb with an unaltered Bbmaj7 lands exactly as the plan asks. My only reservation is bar 46, where Cø7 imports a Bb-minor implication (and a Gb against the melody's A4) just where the plan wants bars 45-46 to stay close to the original ii-V; I put the plain F7 back. Everything else I left untouched.

changes.why: Plain F7 keeps the melody C5/A4 as 5th and 3rd, avoiding the Cø7's Gb and its stray minor-key implication.

review.verdict: Bars 1–24: The tritone-sub program is applied with a clear logic and the chromatic bass lines (Dm-Db-C, Cm-B-Bb) are idiomatic, with the tonic arrivals left plain so the form still reads. My one complaint is bars 12-13, where D7 on beat 3 of bar 12 is immediately followed by another D7 in bar 13, killing the bass motion just as the drive to the first full cadence starts. I restored Ab7 there, which keeps the plan's backdoor pull and lets the line fall Eb-Ab-D-Db-C-B-Bb into bar 16. Bars 25–44: The tritone plan is executed cleanly and the bass lines it produces are excellent: D-Db-C through bars 29-31, E-Eb into the bridge, and the A-Ab-G-Gb-F descent across bars 41-44 is exactly the peak the plan asked for. My only reservation is the near-monoculture of tritone subs, with the diatonic bars left untouched as plain seventh chords. I added the related-ii on bar 26 so the I7 gets a two-chord approach and the technique mix broadens without touching density limits or runs. Bars 45–64: The part reads well: the chromatic B7/Db7 chain through bars 45-48 lands cleanly on a recognizable F7, the last A stays plain before the B7 color in bar 52, and the final Db7-B7-Bbmaj7 cadence is exactly what the plan asked for. Density stays comfortably inside target and no run grows.
